root_cause.text: `udp4_gro_complete()` in the GRO completion path incorrectly relied on `skb->encapsulation` always being cleared, so when encapsulated packets arrived with that flag still set it used the inner network offset instead of the outer one to compute the UDP pseudo-checksum.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `skb->encapsulation = 0;` in `net/core/gro.c` before GRO completion and the CVE description says the “udp GRO complete stage assumes that all the packets inserted the RX have the `encapsulation` flag zeroed,” but in reality NICs, tun, and veth can set it, causing `udp4_gro_complete()` to use the “wrong network offset (inner instead of outer)” and trigger checksum validation errors.

intent_record.intent_summary: Clear the skb encapsulation flag during GRO completion so encapsulated packets fed by NICs are handled correctly.
intent_record.what: A comment and a single assignment were added in gro_complete(): before taking the RCU read lock and iterating protocol handlers, the code now explicitly sets `skb->encapsulation = 0` with a comment stating that NICs can feed encapsulated packets into GRO.
intent_record.how: This clears the skb encapsulation flag before GRO completion handling, preventing the packet from being treated as encapsulated during subsequent protocol completion processing. That changes how downstream protocol handlers interpret the packet metadata and avoids incorrect encapsulation-aware behavior for GRO-fed packets.

grouping_result.intent: Clear the skb encapsulation flag during GRO completion so encapsulated packets fed by NICs are handled correctly.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause by clearing skb->encapsulation during GRO completion, fixing the incorrect pseudo-checksum calculation for encapsulated UDP packets.

candidates.rationale: This is the GRO completion dispatch path where encapsulation state must be handled before protocol-specific completion runs; the bug stems from missing clearing of skb->encapsulation before this completion logic, causing later checksum handling to use the wrong network offset.

This loop represents the GRO completion path in which the skb is handed to protocol callbacks. The vulnerability manifests here because the packet still has skb->encapsulation set when entering completion, leading to incorrect pseudo-checksum computation.

vuln_statements.explanation: This GRO completion dispatch condition is reached while skb->encapsulation may still be set. Because the flag was not cleared before protocol-specific completion, later UDP GRO checksum handling could use the inner network offset instead of the outer one.
